req.title: Player update persists to DB
req.statement: The system shall write updates to the players table so subsequent GET calls reflect the modification.

doc.reasoning: The requirement states that PUT /players/{squadNumber} must persist updates to the DB so subsequent GET calls reflect the change. The source reveals a deliberate bug: update_by_squad_number_async always returns False after commit (no True path), causing the route to raise HTTP 500. Tests must cover: (1) positive EP – valid full update returns 204 and GET reflects new data; (2) negative NEG – squad_number mismatch in body vs path returns 400; (3) negative NEG – update on non-existent player returns 404; (4) BVA – boundary squad numbers (1 and 26, the min/max in the dataset); (5) DT – body squad_number matches path but all optional fields are null/omitted; (6) STC – state transition: create then update then GET verifies persistence. The source bug (always returns False) means the 204 positive test will catch the mutation where True/False is swapped. Exact status codes (204, 400, 404, 500) are asserted to kill constant-mutation operators.

tests.name: test_put_valid_player_returns_204_and_get_reflects_update
preconditions: Player with squadNumber=10 exists in DB (Kabir Mary Reddy)
App is running in-process via TestClient
expected: GET returns HTTP 200 with updated firstName and lastName
tests.executable:
from main import app
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient
client = TestClient(app)

def test_put_valid_player_returns_204_and_get_reflects_update():
    payload = {
        "firstName": "UpdatedFirst",
        "middleName": "UpdatedMiddle",
        "lastName": "UpdatedLast",
        "dateOfBirth": "1990-06-15T00:00:00.000Z",
        "squadNumber": 10,
        "position": "Left Winger",
        "abbrPosition": "LW",
        "team": "Arsenal",
        "league": "Premier League",
        "starting11": True
    }
    put_resp = client.put("/players/squadnumber/10", json=payload)
    assert put_resp.status_code == 204
    get_resp = client.get("/players/squadnumber/10")
    assert get_resp.status_code == 200
    body = get_resp.json()
    assert body["firstName"] == "UpdatedFirst"
    assert body["lastName"] == "UpdatedLast"
    assert body["squadNumber"] == 10
    assert body["position"] == "Left Winger"
    assert body["starting11"] == True

tests.name: test_put_state_transition_create_update_get
preconditions: No player with squadNumber=27 exists in DB
App is running in-process via TestClient
actions: POST /players/ to create player with squadNumber=27
expected: GET returns HTTP 200 with updated firstName and position
tests.executable:
from main import app
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient
client = TestClient(app)

def test_put_state_transition_create_update_get():
    create_payload = {
        "firstName": "NewPlayer",
        "middleName": None,
        "lastName": "TestLast",
        "dateOfBirth": "2000-01-01T00:00:00.000Z",
        "squadNumber": 27,
        "position": "Goalkeeper",
        "abbrPosition": "GK",
        "team": "Test FC",
        "league": "Test League",
        "starting11": False
    }
    post_resp = client.post("/players/", json=create_payload)
    assert post_resp.status_code == 201
    update_payload = {
        "firstName": "UpdatedPlayer",
        "middleName": None,
        "lastName": "UpdatedLast",
        "dateOfBirth": "2001-05-10T00:00:00.000Z",
        "squadNumber": 27,
        "position": "Right-Back",
        "abbrPosition": "RB",
        "team": "Updated FC",
        "league": "Updated League",
        "starting11": True
    }
    put_resp = client.put("/players/squadnumber/27", json=update_payload)
    assert put_resp.status_code == 204
    get_resp = client.get("/players/squadnumber/27")
    assert get_resp.status_code == 200
    body = get_resp.json()
    assert body["firstName"] == "UpdatedPlayer"
    assert body["lastName"] == "UpdatedLast"
    assert body["position"] == "Right-Back"
    assert body["starting11"] == True
    assert body["squadNumber"] == 27
